summary: Social.docx Issue #9 (Supplier↔Warehouse assignments) verified end-to-end. Backend pytest 8/8 pass — GET returns {supplier,assignments,eligible} with is_assigned booleans; POST is idempotent (re-POST updates the row, doesn't 409); is_primary=true demotes other primaries; DELETE returns 204 and 404 on missing rows; cross-country POST returns 400 {code:'cross_country_denied'} (verified by temporarily seeding an LR warehouse); audit trail rows written as warehouse_assigned/warehouse_unassigned. Frontend Admin Supplier Applications drawer (/admin/modules/mart/suppliers → Approved bucket → Review on 'DEMO Delta Beverages CI') renders the 'Warehouse assignments' card above 'Audit trail' with all required data-testids working: empty state, eligible-assign, assignment row, make-primary, remove. Full assign → make-primary → assign 2nd wh → promote 2nd (auto-demotes 1st, confirmed via audit trail 'warehouse_assigned … primary=True') → remove both → empty state — all worked. Regression: Approve/Reject/Suspend actions untouched; drawer content intact.
critical_code_review_comments: admin_assign_supplier_warehouse: Idempotent POST returns 201 even when updating an existing row — arguably should be 200 for update semantics, but the spec explicitly asks for idempotency without 409 so this is acceptable.

SupplierReviewAudit rows for warehouse_assigned/unassigned intentionally leave from_status/to_status NULL (only 'action' + 'notes' encoded). Consumers should be aware — the AdminSupplierApplications drawer currently renders those correctly (no arrow shown when from_status is missing).

The 'Make primary' button demotes existing primaries via a silent UPDATE (no separate audit action for the demotion). If auditability of demotion matters, consider writing a second audit row when a demotion occurs. Not a blocker.

The DELETE unassign endpoint does NOT re-elect a new primary when the removed row was the primary — supplier can end up with 0 primaries. Backend tests do not cover this edge case; UI shows no warning. Consider whether one-primary auto-election on delete is desired.

rca of the issue: N/A — feature works as designed. Idempotent POST correctly avoids 409, one-primary invariant maintained on assign (but not on delete), and audit rows are written with the migration-relaxed CHECK constraint.
